prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished, production-quality website design comp for the GTP 2026 subpage "ON THE NEWS". Render the website itself edge to edge, landscape aspect ratio approximately 3:2 at high resolution, no browser window, phone, device frame, desk, or collage of versions. This is a vibrant, celebratory showcase of press articles, with images and readable headlines that link out to the publishers, not an article-detail page. Use the attached existing GTP Media screenshot ONLY as a reference for its slim pill-shaped GTP navigation, Poppins heading type, Inter body type, and recognizable GTP identity. Do NOT carry over that screenshot's full-background photo hero, Media title, or dark photograph overlays. This is a NEW page composition.

Visual world: GTP dark teal #093a48, turquoise #009CB4, lime #86BC25 and orange #f06a00, sophisticated smooth multi-colour gradients across the page ground. Make the background visibly a blended gradient, not a flat solid colour. Rich warm event energy, generous photographic scale, strong readable editorial hierarchy. No purple, neon, glassmorphism, 3D ornaments, confetti over text, or generic SaaS equal-card grid. Images are distinct, whole, undistorted photographs contained inside their own clearly defined media regions, with titles and publisher labels beside or below, never painted over the photographs. Use realistic but synthetic diverse conference audiences, speakers and climate/nature scenes as placeholder article imagery, not photographs of recognizable public figures. Precise professional spacing and aligned controls, generous but purposeful whitespace. Body text at readable size.

Include real functional UI affordances: thin existing-style GTP navigation along top with "Home", "About", "Programme", "Speakers", "Media", "Get Involved"; "Media / On the News" breadcrumb; very legible bold "ON THE NEWS" title; short intro "Stories, ideas and coverage from GTP 2026 and beyond."; external arrow icon and "Read article" on articles. Include a small but readable caption "DESIGN CONCEPT - SAMPLE CONTENT" so invented example coverage is unmistakably illustrative. No claims of actual publisher coverage, no fabricated quotes, awards, readership or statistics. Example article texts are labelled "Sample article" with generic "Example publication" as publisher, and no invented dates. Shared story headline examples: "The conversations shaping positive tipping points", "From understanding to collective action", "New perspectives on a thriving planet". Photographs and headlines must be the main visual proof; the title must not eat the entire first viewport. Show the beginning of the article archive below the opening experience, with "Explore all articles", filter controls "All", "GTP conference", "Other articles", and a proper "Search articles" input. Keep this work as a credible designed live webpage rather than a poster. Do not add any concept explanation outside the page.
COMPOSITION 1 - SELECTABLE SPOTLIGHT. This is an interactive editorial showcase, not an equal-card grid. After the compact masthead and page title, show a dominant clickable article stage occupying approximately two thirds of the content width: one large whole 16:9 photograph of a warmly lit conference plenary with a diverse seated audience and a teal stage, and below it a white high-contrast integrated headline matte containing the first exact example headline, small "Sample article / Example publication", and "Read article ↗". To its RIGHT is a crisp narrow spotlight selector containing THREE compact image-thumbnail and headline BUTTON rows, not separate large cards. Give the first selector a plainly selected state with a lime rule and a small "Selected" marker; second and third rows remain quiet. A section label "In the spotlight" and subtle "01 / 03" show deliberate selection. This short selector controls the main story preview; clicking the large photo-and-title opens the article. The whole feature composition should have editorial scale with nearly unrounded image corners and no heavy card framing. Ground is a confident deep teal into turquoise gradient, a distinct soft lime glow towards the lower right, and a warm orange light area at an outer edge; the main white headline matte creates clear reading contrast. At bottom, show the beginning of "Explore all articles" and a genuine search/filter toolbar plus the upper part of a few varied image-led article entries. The visitor immediately sees a featured story and how to choose the next one.
approval: User selected Option 1 and authorized implementation on 13 October 2026
